The arrow

Anatomy

The geometry is locked. It carries a positive, forward-moving connotation.

Download Start Cap SVG Download End Cap SVG
Every arrow in the system
is this one shape, stretched.

SolidThe default. Solid Orange.

OutlineUsed for badges and quieter surfaces.

Using the arrow

The same shape does six other jobs. Each has a fixed role, so the arrow always means the same thing wherever it appears.

health_and_safety Workforce readiness

Eyebrow badgeOutline arrow, orange text, above hero headlines and as a section kicker. Works well with icons.

Partner with us arrow_forward

CTACTAs should be in the arrow to create emphasis.

010203

Number and icon chipsThe squarer chip. A glyph inside fills about 60% of the chip optically, big and confident, never floating small in the middle.

Portrait containerThe cutout clips to the arrow on the bottom half only. Head and shoulders are never clipped and jut freely above.

Rounded Rectangle

The arrow can soften into a rounded rectangle for specific UI containers.

[ Graphic Pending: Rounded Rectangle Use ]

Journey and list rows

The arrow reads as a sequence. Chained left to right, each stage nests into the next — one continuous path from first contact to the ward. The same shape, repeated, carries the whole journey.

Use in data

The arrow naturally translates to quantitative data. Use it for horizontal bar charts to convey momentum and direction alongside the metrics.

Comparative metricsUse solid orange for NewMed Skills data, and outline for industry averages or competitors.

Volume or rankingAdjust the opacity of the arrow to indicate hierarchy or descending volume.

Incorrect usage

The arrow is the identity. Distorting it or scattering it costs more than any other misuse in this manual.

✗Ready
Don't highlight one wordTwo words minimum, always.
✗We move them across
Don't stack highlightsOne highlight per headline.
✗
Don't stretch the shapeThe radius and point are locked to the height.
✗
Don't recolour freelyOrange, amber, the gradient, cream, white, ink and maroon only.
✗
Don't scatter itOne dominant arrow per composition, not a pattern of small ones.
✗
Don't rotateThe arrow always points right, level with the baseline.
